x: Low literacy, poor health and few industries are the listed signs of infrastructural and social backwardness. Item 4 is the opposite: regionalism grows from uneven industrialisation (Bombay and West Bengal held 59% of capital in 1948), not industry concentrated in every region. So '1, 2 and 3 only'.

All four are correct: Zone I was North Andhra, Zone II East Godavari-West Godavari-Krishna, Zone III Guntur-Prakasam-Nellore and Zone IV Rayalaseema; Zones V and VI were the Telangana zones that went to Telangana in 2014, Zone VI including Hyderabad.

All three pairs are correct: AP's 2019 Act reserved 75% of private industrial jobs for locals (the first such law), Haryana's 2020 Act 75% of private jobs up to a salary ceiling (struck down by the Punjab and Haryana High Court in Nov 2023), and Jharkhand's 2021 Act 75% of lower-salary private jobs.
All four are correct as per PLFS 2023-24: AP youth unemployment was 17.5% (well above the national rate), rural 15.5%, urban 22.7%, and urban female youth 29.1%.

Pairs 1, 2 and 4 are correct: Patidar agitation 2015, Jallikattu 2016-17, and the Anna Hazare movement is listed among other youth movements. Pair 3 is wrong: the Nirbhaya protests followed the December 2012 Delhi gang-rape; 1974 is the year of the Nav Nirman and JP movements.

Illiteracy, malnutrition, poor health care and lack of safe water and sanitation are the listed social indicators of poverty. Size of the house is not one; UPPSC 2025 keyed it as the NOT-a-social-indicator option.

The Tendulkar Committee (report 2009) dropped the calorie anchor, used the Mixed Reference Period (MRP), applied the urban basket to both sectors and included health and education spending. The other options are wrong: it did not use a rural-only basket, exclude non-food spending or restore the calorie anchor.
